title: CrossCheck: Evidence-Based Compliance Verification for OT Network Segmentation
content: Checking whether an operational technology (OT) network satisfies a segmentation standard takes four to six weeks by hand: passive monitoring for an asset inventory, then a manual check against firewall rules. The gap is sharpest in water and wastewater, facing a December 31, 2026 deadline for Emergency Response Plans under the America's Water Infrastructure Act (AWIA), where the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) finds inadequate boundary protection is its most common weakness. We built CrossCheck, a tool that answers it from evidence an operator already has: flow data and whatever policy governs it, inline rules or an access list. From those inputs it checks three of the four elements in CISA's Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goal 3.I, Network Segmentation: boundary devices between segments, inter-segment traffic tight enough to contain a breach, and physical isolation where required. On a small, hand-built set, CrossCheck caught every planted violation and correctly flagged insufficient evidence; a keyword baseline for manual practice missed a real violation and guessed rather than admit it didn't know. Asset classification and the standard's contextual exception clause are out of scope; the design generalizes beyond water and wastewater to any OT sector built around VLAN segments behind a boundary device.
